==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{der|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|fro|contract}}, from {{der|en|la|contractus|pos=noun}}, from {{m|la|contraho|contrahere|to bring together, to bring about, to conclude a bargain}} [from {{m|la|con-||with, together}} + {{m|la|traho|trahere|to draw, to pull}}] {{suf|la|nocat=1||-tus<pos:suffix forming nouns from verbs>}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|kŏn'trăkt}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɒntɹækt/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɔntɹakt/|a=SSB}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-contract.ogg|a=SSB}}
** {{audio|en|en-uk-contract (noun).ogg|a=SSB}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑntɹækt/|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-contract-noun.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɔntɹækt/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɒntɹɛkt/|a=NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɔntɾakt/|a=Scotland}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɒntɾakt/|a=Wales}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# An [[agreement]] between two or more parties, to perform a specific [[job]] or [[work]] order, often [[temporary]] or of fixed [[duration]] and usually governed by a written agreement.
#: {{syn|en|compact|pact}}
#: {{coi|en|sign a '''contract'''}}
#: {{coi|en|write up a '''contract'''}}
#: {{coi|en|read a '''contract'''}}
#: {{coi|en|countersign a '''contract'''}}
#: {{coi|en|legally-binding '''contract'''}}
#: {{coi|en|unwritten '''contract'''}}
#: {{ux|en|Marriage is a '''contract'''.}}
#: {{co|en|hired on a short-term '''contract'''}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-10|volume=408|issue=8848|author=Lexington
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/united-states/21583274-new-wave-press-barons-should-not-allow-newspapers-become-niche-products-keeping Keeping the mighty honest]
|passage=British journalists shun complete respectability, feeling a duty to be ready to savage the mighty, or rummage through their bins. Elsewhere in Europe, government '''contracts''' and subsidies ensure that press barons will only defy the mighty so far.}}
## A period of work agreed to under a temporary contract.
##: {{ux|en|He worked a six-month '''contract''' on an oil rig.}}
# {{lb|en|legal}} An [[agreement]] which the [[law]] will [[enforce]] in some way. A [[legally]] [[binding]] contract must [[contain]] at least one [[promise]], i.e., a [[commitment]] or [[offer]], by an [[offeror]] to and [[accepted]] by an [[offeree]] to do something in the [[future]]. A contract is thus [[executory]] rather than [[executed]].
# {{lb|en|legal}} The [[document]] containing such an agreement.
# {{lb|en|legal}} A part of legal studies dealing with [[law]]s and [[jurisdiction]] related to contracts.
# {{lb|en|informal}} An order, usually given to a hired [[assassin]], to kill someone.
#: {{ux|en|The mafia boss put a '''contract''' out on the man who betrayed him.}}
# {{lb|en|bridge}} The declarer's [[undertaking]] to win the number of [[tricks]] bid with a stated suit as trump.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1955|year_published=1959|author=w:Ian Fleming|title={{w|Moonraker (novel)|Moonraker}}|volume=|location=London|publisher=Pan Books|chapter=Cards With A Stranger|page=47|passage=On Meyer's deal they went one down in five diamonds, but on the next hand M. opened four spades and Bond's three small trumps and an outside king, queen were all M. needed for the '''contract'''.}}

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|-}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Contracted; affianced; betrothed.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1609|author=w:William Shakespeare|title=w:Sonnet 1|passage=But thou, '''contracted''' to thine own bright eyes, feed'st thy light's flame with self-substantial fuel}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Not abstract; [[concrete]].
#* {{RQ:Recorde Whetstone|passage=But now in eche kinde of these, there are certaine nombers named ''Abſtracte'': and other called nombers '''''Contracte'''''.}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{der|en|enm|-}}, from {{der|en|frm|contracter}}, from {{der|en|la|contractum}}, past participle of {{m|la|contraho|contrahere|to bring together, to bring about, to conclude a bargain}}, from {{m|la|con-||with, together}} + {{m|la|traho|trahere|to draw, to pull}}. The verb developed after the noun, and originally meant only "draw together"; the sense "make a contract with" developed later.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|kəntrăkt}}, {{IPA|en|/kənˈtɹækt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-contract-verb2.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-uk-contract (verb).ogg|a=UK}}
* {{rhymes|en|ækt|s=2}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To draw [[together]] or [[nearer]]; to [[shorten]], [[narrow]], or [[lessen]].
#: {{ux|en|The snail’s body '''contracted''' into its shell.}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''contract''' one’s sphere of action}}
#: {{ux|en|Private property investment expands while protections for lower-income residents '''contract'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Allestree Tongue|section=Of Boasting|page=168|passage=We ſee in all things how deſuetude do's '''contract''' and narrow our faculties, ſo that we may apprehend only thoſe things wherein we are converſant.}}
#* {{RQ:Wordsworth Yarrow Revisited|poem=The Armenian Lady's Love|stanza=18|page=102|passage=Mutual was the sudden transport; / Breathless questions followed fast, / Years '''contracting''' to a moment, / Each word greedier than the last; {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|grammar}} To shorten by omitting a letter or letters or by reducing two or more vowels or syllables to one.
#: {{ux|en|The word “cannot” is often '''contracted''' into “can’t”.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To make an agreement or contract; to [[covenant]].
#: {{ux|en|The company '''contracted''' with the council to build 200 new houses.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To enter into a contract with (someone or something).
#: {{ux|en|We have just '''contracted''' new pest control services.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To enter into (an agreement) with mutual obligations; to make (an arrangement).
#* {{RQ:Hakluyt Principall Navigations|passage=We have '''contracted''' an inviolable amitie, peace, and league with the aforesaid Queene.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1721|author=w:John Strype|title=Ecclesiastical Memorials
|passage=Many persons {{...}} had '''contracted''' marriage within the degrees of consanguinity {{...}} prohibited by law.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To bring on; to incur; to acquire.
#: {{ux|en|She '''contracted''' the habit of smoking in her teens.}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''contract''' a debt}}
#* {{RQ:Pope Works|volume=I|title=Jervas|page=391|passage=Smit with the love of Siſter-arts we came, / And met congenial, mingling flame with flame; / Like friendly colours found our arts unite, / Each from each '''contract''' new ſtrength and light.}}
#* {{RQ:Swift Works|volume=V|title=An Essay on the Fates of Clergymen|page=113|passage=This talent of discretion, {{...}} is no where so serviceable as to the clergy, to whose preferment nothing is so fatal as the character of wit, politeness in reading or manners, or that kind of behaviour, which we '''contract''' by having too much conversation with persons of high station and eminency; {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis||passage=A love like mine, Sir, I feel, is '''contracted''' once and for ever.|1}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To gain or acquire (an illness).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=Davidson C. Umeh|title=Protect Your Life: A Health Handbook for Law Enforcement Professionals|page=69
|passage=An officer '''contracted''' hepatitis B and died after handling the blood-soaked clothing of a homicide victim {{...}}}}
# To draw together so as to wrinkle; to knit.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello Q1|act=III|scene=iii|page=45|passage=And didſt '''contract''', and purſe thy brow together, / As if thou then hadſt ſhut vp in thy braine, / Some horrible counſell: {{...}}}}
# To [[betroth]]; to [[affiance]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|act=V|scene=v|page=60|column=2|passage=The truth is, ſhe and I (long ſince '''contracted''') / Are now ſo ſure that nothing can diſſolve vs: {{...}}}}
